claims.text: Adjusting the relative concentrations of constituent elements in non-equiatomic HEAs can tune the magnetic transition temperature.
Adjusting the relative concentrations of constituent elements in non-equiatomic HEAs can tune the magnetocaloric effect.
Composition changes tune magnetic and magnetocaloric behavior by modifying exchange interactions among atoms.
The baseline non-equiatomic HEA exhibits a characteristic magnetic transition and magnetocaloric response.
Varying the amount or identity of magnetic elements changes the alloy composition.
Non-equiatomic elemental substitution affects the atomic-scale arrangement and local chemical environment.
Changing alloy composition alters exchange-interaction strengths among constituent atoms.
Altered exchange-interaction strengths shift the magnetic ordering temperature.
Altered exchange interactions modify the magnetic entropy change under an applied magnetic field.
Elemental substitution will cause the magnetic transition temperature to increase or decrease depending on the substitution.
The magnitude of the magnetocaloric effect will change in response to the altered magnetic entropy change.
Compositional tuning is expected to be most pronounced within a range where magnetic interactions are sensitive to elemental changes.
Outside the sensitive compositional range, magnetic sensitivity may diminish.
Outside the sensitive compositional range, secondary phases may form.
The magnitude and direction of changes in transition temperature and magnetocaloric effect depend on which elements are altered.
